Colours of the Figures of PhyloCactus

Source: R/palette.R
phylocactus_colours.Rd

Returns the colours of one role of the palette the package uses for every figure. Each role does one job: "categorical" tells unordered things apart (trees compared, methods, loci, nucleotides), in a fixed order that is never cycled; "outcome" and "state" give the answers of an identification on a diverging scale, blue for a right answer, grey for none, red for a wrong one; "sequential" encodes a magnitude in greys, from light to dark; "support" gives the classes of bootstrap support of a node as Tutorial 3 draws them, with constrained nodes apart; "neutral" holds the greys of text, lines, rules, backgrounds and the marks of a single series (bars, histograms, segments, points); "theme" holds the colours of theme_phylocactus(); "iucn" keeps the colours of the IUCN Red List categories.

Usage

phylocactus_colours(
  role = c("categorical", "outcome", "state", "sequential", "support", "neutral",
    "theme", "iucn")
)

Arguments

role

Character. One of "categorical", "outcome", "state", "sequential", "support", "neutral", "theme" or "iucn".

Value

A character vector of hexadecimal colours, named by category where the role has categories.

See also

theme_phylocactus(), scale_fill_iucn().

Examples

phylocactus_colours("outcome")
#> species correct   genus correct      abstention   wrong species     wrong genus 
#>       "#1c5cab"       "#86b6ef"       "#a8a79f"       "#ee8a85"       "#b2182b" 
phylocactus_colours("categorical")[1:3]
#>      blue    orange      aqua 
#> "#2a78d6" "#eb6834" "#1baf7a"
